source.title: Is Grokking a Computational Glass Relaxation?
source.authors: Xiaotian Zhang; Yue Shang; Entao Yang; Ge Zhang

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures training and test accuracy on modular arithmetic tasks, including how training conditions affect delayed generalization. It uses a different method and adds entropy-landscape sampling and a new optimizer rather than reproducing the original study’s full recipe.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own modular-arithmetic training outcomes and weight-norm interventions. It discusses mechanisms such as circuit formation but does not measure circuits or continuous circuit-progress measures. Entropy-landscape findings do not measure any of the listed versions directly. Results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study trains the Nanda et al. one-layer transformer on modular arithmetic (p=67, 50% split) and reports its own grokking curves under AdamW. It also reports that a fixed weight norm of 30 and its WanD optimizer remove the delay. The main contribution, entropy-landscape sampling, is a different method aimed at why grokking occurs. Most quantitative outcomes are figure-only.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors frame grokking as computational glass relaxation and find no entropy barrier, rejecting the first-order phase-transition account. They report a large high-entropy advantage that shrinks when the norm is fixed. They argue grokking is caused by optimization dynamics: WanD removes it and finds high-norm generalizing solutions, which challenges a weight-norm-only (Goldilocks) account.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a one-layer transformer and modular arithmetic following Nanda et al.; uses modulus 67 and a 50% split for the main experiments, and adds entropy sampling, fixed-norm experiments, and WanD optimizer training.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome changes with optimizer (AdamW versus WanD), fixed weight norm 30, task difficulty, and training-set fraction. WanD is described as sensitive to hyperparameters.

fits_no_version.finding: Entropy landscapes over train loss and test accuracy show no entropy barrier between memorization and generalization. The equilibrium curve is continuous, which the authors read as contradicting a first-order phase transition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking is not a first-order phase transition but a slow relaxation from a non-equilibrium (glassy) memorizing state.

fits_no_version.finding: Max-entropy states at a given train loss generalize far better than AdamW states (a high-entropy advantage). This advantage is much weaker when grokking is removed by fixing the norm.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking networks sit far from equilibrium; how far correlates with the generalization delay.

record.problems: The main study is limited to one-layer transformers on modular arithmetic tasks. Most accuracy curves are presented in figures without exact values in the text; no uncertainty estimates are reported. WanD is described by the authors as a proof of concept, sensitive to hyperparameters, and unstable near generalization.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: How the delay grows as the training set shrinks. The 50–80% sweeps are figure-only with no stated delays.
Non-algorithmic data (images, text, molecules) and initialization-scale / lazy-to-rich switching.
Circuit efficiency, critical dataset size and ungrokking.
Adaptive-optimizer instabilities and floating-point/softmax limits as specific mechanisms.
Not tested: no circuit or progress measures.

missing.what: General statement that WanD has an efficiency advantage in tasks with severe grokking, and still generalizes ahead of AdamW where grokking is largely gone.
Appendix B.3 text implying that grokking is greatly eliminated at higher training fractions. This bears on the dataset-size dependence but is not quantified.

record.verdict_notes: Reader mislabelled r4–r6 as V5 evidence (they test V3's weight-norm switch) and r13–r24 as V1. Reader also gave a limits_scope label to figure-only sweeps, which should be untested. Nanda et al. is an original source, but this study is a separate replication on p=67, so it is not excluded. Fig. 3 states AdamW also generalizes by about 2,000 steps, making the r7 delay contrast unclear.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test how delay changes as the training set shrinks in a controlled comparison with otherwise fixed conditions, except for plotted dataset-split sweeps whose condition-specific values are not stated in the text.
No generalizing circuit, Fourier algorithm, memorizing component, or continuous circuit-progress measure is tracked.
Only modular arithmetic tasks are studied; no non-algorithmic data or lazy-to-rich initialization-scale sweep is tested.
No LLM pretraining or realistic-data fine-tuning is studied.
The study does not test a critical dataset size or an ungrokking threshold below it, and does not measure whether a more efficient circuit is selected.
The study does not identify or compare learned algorithms across runs, architectures, or hyperparameters.
The study changes optimizer, but does not test adaptive-optimizer instabilities or floating-point/softmax numerical limits as artifacts.

rows.value: Grokking is largely eliminated; WanD and AdamW have comparable performance and achieve generalization after approximately 2,000 optimization steps.
rows.note: The paper also reports WanD taking about 50 seconds per 1K steps, versus roughly 72 seconds for AdamW on one GeForce RTX 4090 GPU.

rows.operation_detail: Measured parameter weight norm during WanD training
rows.measure: weight norm at generalization
rows.value: The weight norm continued to increase and eventually reached about 175; the model generalized at high weight norm.
rows.note: The authors present this as a counterexample to attributing grokking solely to weight-norm evolution toward the Goldilocks zone.
rows.check: Under WanD, with no weight decay, the model generalizes at a weight norm of about 175. This runs opposite to a low-norm generalizing solution. It does not show that weight decay fails to favour efficient circuits under AdamW.
